passage: In nature, few species exist in isolation; instead, organisms constantly interact through intricate networks of competition, predation, and mutualism. A classic example of mutualism occurs between acacia trees and certain species of stinging ants in tropical regions. The acacia provides the ants with shelter inside hollow thorns and nutritious nectar from specialized glands, while the ants fiercely defend the tree against herbivorous insects, browsing mammals, and even encroaching vines that might block sunlight. When ecologists experimentally removed the ants from acacia trees, the plants quickly suffered severe leaf damage and were overgrown by neighboring vegetation. This partnership illustrates how coevolution can bind two vastly different organisms into a single functional unit, where the survival of each partner depends directly on the thriving of the other.
